status_note: US EPA project calls the POI-5-only API IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride in production; both POI 4.1.2 and 5.2.3 appear at the commit, suggesting this commit is itself the 4->5 transition (bump + adaptation together). NOT yet differential-verified.
discovery_method: Phase 2 external mining: GitHub code search for 'setByteArrayMaxOverride' (call, not definition), then history check.

behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: POI 5.0 added a default maximum byte-array size in IOUtils; reading larger data throws at runtime. Compiles fine against POI 5 -> behavioural. Fix raises the limit via the POI-5-only IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride(n).

adaptation.author: AA\TMARTI02
adaptation.summary: Raised POI's byte-array limit to ~200 MB to process large data files under POI 5's stricter default cap.

verification.differential_needed: Build repo, apply POI 4->5 to pre-adaptation code, confirm the byte-limit break manifests and that setByteArrayMaxOverride resolves it (or a generated mimic test).
verification.standalone_repro_note: A standalone mimic (IOUtils.toByteArray with a large declared length) was attempted 2026-07-01 and did NOT reproduce the break: POI's byte cap is enforced deep in its document/record parsing, not at the top-level API (toByteArray just allocates until OOM). A faithful repro needs a crafted document or the repo's own parsing path (repo build required). Unlike xstream's one-call ForbiddenClassException, this parser-internal break is not standalone-reproducible.
verification.conclusion: Signature-confirmed POI-5 production adaptation; full BBC verification pending (standalone mimic insufficient - see standalone_repro_note).
